newsitem.title: USA: Quaker Q2 food income up before charge.
newsitem.headline: Quaker Q2 food income up before charge.

text.p: Quaker Oats Co said Thursday its total foods operating income, excluding a restructuring charge, rose to $79.5 million, up from $70.8 million a year ago.
Including a $10.7 million pretax restructuring charge for the consolidation of its Brazilian pasta manufacturing operations, Quaker's total foods operating income was $68.8 million.
Total foods sales were $780.7 million, up six percent from $736.8 million a year ago.

U.S. and Canadian foods operating income was $76.8 milion, up 15 percent from $66.6 million a year ago. Volume increases were recorded in ready-to-eat cereal, up 39 percent; hot cereals, up seven percent; Aunt Jemima mixes and syrups, up 15 percent; and Golden Grain, up three percent.

These increases more than offset the operating income effect of June 1996 ready-to-eat cereal price reductions, a significant operating income decline in rice cakes, and higher advertising and merchandising expenses.

Boxed ready-to-eat cereals posted 25 percent volume growth. Quaker's value-priced bagged cereals nearly doubled in volume and grew to more than a two percent share of the $8.0 billion ready-to-eat cereal category.
International foods operating loss for the quarter was $8.0 million after a $10.7 million pretax charge, compared with operating income of $4.2 million a year ago.

Total beverage operating income in the second quarter was $93.7 million, including a $1.1 million pretax restructuring charge for the closing of an office in Singapore, compared with $91.3 million a year ago.

Worldwide Gatorade sales of $538.9 million were up three percent from a year ago. International Gatorade sales rose 19 percent, while U.S. sales were "virtually flat" due to cooler, wetter spring weather across the country in May, Quaker said.
U.S. and Canadian beverage operating income dropped five percent to $90.6 million due mainly to increased spending to introduce the new Gatorade Frost sports beverage line.

"While the U.S. weather in May slowed Gatorade's volume growth in the quarter, its year-to-date trend is strong with sales up six percent and operating income up 26 percent," William Smithburg, chairman, said in a statement. "Gatorade's operating income, operating margins and market share have expanded."
He added that the new Gatorade Frost line already has more market share than Gatorade's closest competitor.
Quaker said recently that the three-flavor Gatorade Frost line, launched in January, hit the $100 million sales market earlier this month, after only six months in the market.
